claim_verdicts.evidence: options.md: "The Interface Segregation Principle (ISP) or Encapsulation: Scenarios (classes) that depend on configuration settings depend only on the configuration settings that they use." Same principle (depend only on what you use); the lesson's split-into-small-interfaces half follows directly and is outline item 1.

interfaces.md: "A class or struct that implements an interface must provide implementations for all declared members (unless the interface provides a default implementation)." interface.md: "Member bodies in an interface are the *default implementation*." None of IFullNotifier's three members has a body (NotifierIspViolation.cs:7-12 @ stage-1). Round 2 wording "every method IFullNotifier declares — all three" holds for this interface.

Ran: stage-1 NotifierIspViolation.cs with Retry changed to Retry(int orderId, int attempt), dotnet build (SDK 10, net10.0) -> "error CS0535: 'SmsOnlyNotifier' does not implement interface member 'IFullNotifier.Retry(int, int)'". Docs: "must provide an Equals method that matches the interface signature".

git show stage-1:samples/DonHang.Samples/Samples/Design/NotifierIspViolation.cs lines 7-26: three members as stated; Send => Console.WriteLine($"sms about order {orderId}: {subject}"); History => throw new NotSupportedException("this channel keeps no history"); Retry => throw new NotSupportedException("this channel does not retry").

INotifier.cs:5-8 declares only void Send(int orderId, string subject). NotifierBase.cs:5 "public abstract class NotifierBase : INotifier", :18 "protected abstract string Format(int orderId, string subject);", EmailNotifier and SmsNotifier (:21, :27) override only Format.

Ran: static void Use(IFullNotifier n); Use(new SmsNotifier()); against stage-1 sources, dotnet build -> "error CS1503: Argument 1: cannot convert from 'DonHang.Samples.Oop.SmsNotifier' to 'DonHang.Samples.Design.IFullNotifier'". UseSmall(INotifier) with SmsNotifier/EmailNotifier produced no error.
claim_verdicts.source: local build in scratchpad against examples/don-hang @ stage-1

claim_verdicts.evidence: Follows from code: IFullNotifier exposes History() publicly to any holder (interface members without body are implicitly public, interface.md:30) and SmsOnlyNotifier.History throws NotSupportedException (NotifierIspViolation.cs:21-22); nothing in the type tells the caller which implementation it holds.

Design reasoning derived from the ISP definition in claim 1 (per-dependent need, not method count); worded conditionally in the lesson ("fine when every caller and every implementer needs all three"). No factual/version content.

git show stage-1:samples/DonHang.Samples/Samples/Design/NotifierIspViolation.cs line 14: "// SmsNotifier only ever sends. It still has to answer for History and Retry —"; line 16: "public sealed class SmsOnlyNotifier : IFullNotifier". The comment sits directly above SmsOnlyNotifier and names SmsNotifier.

issues.text: "crashes" states more than the code shows. SmsOnlyNotifier.History throws NotSupportedException (claim 4); whether the hypothetical support screen crashes depends on whether it handles the exception, which the lesson does not show. The q4 context can keep "crashes" because it describes one screen's outcome as a given scenario.
issues.quote: and a support screen that asks any `IFullNotifier` for its `History()` crashes the first time it is handed this one
issues.fix: Replace "crashes the first time it is handed this one" with "gets a `NotSupportedException` the first time it is handed this one".

issues.text: "Both" comes right after two classes are named (EmailNotifier and SmsNotifier), so I first read it as those two classes, not the two designs. The next sentence ("A fat interface hurts on two sides") did not settle it.
issues.quote: and `EmailNotifier` and `SmsNotifier` derive from `NotifierBase`. Both live in the samples today.
issues.fix: Replace "Both live in the samples today." with "Both designs live in the samples today."

issues.text: Misconception 2 states the belief with its own rebuttal inside ("not about who is forced to depend on it"), so no one would say it that way. The correction's "a small count is a symptom, not the goal" made me stop: a symptom sounds like a sign of a problem, but here a small count is the good result.
issues.quote: "ISP is only about how many methods an interface has, not about who is forced to depend on it." → Actually a small count is a symptom, not the goal.
issues.fix: Reword the belief to "ISP means every interface should have as few methods as possible." and replace "a small count is a symptom, not the goal" with "a small count is often the result, not the rule".

issues.text: q1 (carried over from round 1): options b and c are false on their face to anyone who has seen IFullNotifier or any class implementing an interface, and d is off-topic. I can pick a without reading section 4.
issues.quote: An interface in C# may declare at most one method
issues.fix: Replace b or c with a distractor from the lesson, e.g. "Its `Send` method has the wrong parameters for `IFullNotifier`".

issues.text: q4 option c explanation: "would matter when you gave up on the interface" reads as if checking names is sometimes right, which confused me more than the option did. The rest of the sentence is clear.
issues.quote: Checking names would matter when you gave up on the interface, but that is the "ask which kind it is" code the earlier lessons warn against.
issues.fix: Replace with: "Checking names is what you do when you stop trusting the interface; that is the \"ask which kind it is\" code the earlier lessons warn against." (en and vi).
